Paragraph:
Translation: Not by merely abstaining from work can one achieve freedom from reaction, nor by renunciation alone can one attain perfection.

Purport (Excerpt): The renounced order of life can be accepted upon being purified by the discharge of the prescribed form of duties... Without purification, one cannot attain success by abruptly adopting the fourth order of life (sannyasa)... Without purification of heart, sannyasa is simply a disturbance to the social order...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The false belief that external inaction or running away from duties automatically cleanses internal baggage or creates spiritual perfection.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna refutes passive renunciation: simply stopping work or donning the robes of a renunciant does not free a person from emotional reactions or internal impurities.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna is disabused of the notion that quitting his duty as a warrior will magically grant him inner peace or liberation.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Futility of Passive Avoidance: Realizing that stopping activity does not stop mental distress
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Superficial Coping vs. Real Change: Changing external circumstances without purifying internal motives
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Premature Withdrawal: Attempting to retreat from life before achieving emotional maturity

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Mere physical cessation of work does not yield freedom from karmic reactions, nor does adopting external renunciation (sannyasa) grant perfection without internal heart-purification. True renunciation is an internal state reached through dedicated service, not external withdrawal.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Quitting your job, isolating yourself, or stepping away from responsibilities does not resolve internal conflict. Emotional healing cannot be achieved through passive avoidance. If the mind remains unpurified, external retreat only transports the same anxieties to a quieter location.
